landmarks.name: Dana Porter Library
facts: It is the main library for the arts, humanities and social sciences.
It is named after a Chief Justice of Ontario who served as the university's chancellor in the 1960s.

landmarks.name: Claudette Millar Hall
facts: The university named this residence in November 2017, shortly after it opened.

landmarks.name: United College
facts: It hosts the Waterloo Indigenous Student Centre.
Founded in 1962 by a Protestant church as St. Paul's University College, it took its current name in 2022.

landmarks.name: Renison University College
facts: Its English Language Institute has taught English as a second language since 1970.
It is an Anglican college; Ontario issued Letters Patent in 2010 confirming its current official name.

landmarks.name: J. R. Coutts Engineering Lecture Hall
Ira G. Needles Hall
facts: It houses the Registrar's Office.

landmarks.name: Modern Languages
facts: It houses the Theatre of the Arts.

landmarks.name: J. G. Hagey Hall of the Humanities
facts: It is named after the university's first president.

landmarks.name: Earth Sciences & Chemistry
facts: It is joined to Biology 1 by The Link, whose third floor once held a student lounge and exam bank.

landmarks.name: Mathematics & Computer
facts: It is home to the MathSoc C&D coffee shop and the Comfy Lounge.

landmarks.name: Physics
facts: Its department includes Donna Strickland, who won the 2018 Nobel Prize for chirped pulse amplification.

landmarks.name: Biology 1
facts: The Science Society's student coffee shop, C&D, runs out of it.

landmarks.name: School of Optometry & Vision Science
facts: It is home to Canada's only English-language school for training eye doctors.

landmarks.name: B.C. Matthews Hall
facts: It is named after the university's third president.

landmarks.name: Engineering 5

landmarks.name: Tatham Centre
facts: It is the hub for co-operative education and career services.

facts: It is the oldest building erected for the university, put up in 1958.

landmarks.name: Mike & Ophelia Lazaridis Quantum-Nano Centre
facts: One wing's windows vary in reflectivity to symbolise superposition; the other has a honeycomb pattern inspired by carbon.

landmarks.name: Centre for Environmental and Information Technology

facts: It is named after a former dean of the faculty.

landmarks.name: Mathematics 3

facts: It is a main building of the Cheriton School, named after a former Premier of Ontario.

landmarks.name: Student Life Centre
facts: It is open around the clock and houses the Turnkey Desk.

landmarks.name: South Campus Hall
facts: It houses the campus bookstore and the W Store.

facts: It was built as a student-run pub and events venue.

facts: Its gyms double as the big exam halls at the end of each term.
In 2017, ground broke on a joint 63,000-square-foot expansion of it and the Student Life Centre.

landmarks.name: Feridun Hamdullahpur Field House
facts: It is named after a former president of the university.
It hosted the CFL Invitational Combine every year from 2023 to 2026.
